Subject: Production tail latency surge & fair-share collapse on Medicore VPC

Hannah —

We started seeing a sharp P95/P99 latency increase across our private VPC at ~13:20 PDT, coincident with a sustained rise in 502/5xx rates. Throughput to our inference endpoints dropped ~35% despite steady request volume. Attached are the last-hour timeseries and a short sampled log (502s).

Metrics summary (13:20–13:45):
- P95: 480ms -> 1.8s
- P99: 860ms -> 5.4s
- 5xx rate: 0.3% -> 6.2%
- Effective qps: -35%

We are in full production for a time-sensitive rollout; CTO and procurement are watching this. Can you help us triage immediately? Medicore is asking for an exec-level update in the next 45 minutes.

Attachments: medicore-p95-p99-timeseries-20250918.png (image), medicore-sampled-502-logs-14-20.txt (text)

Thanks,
Daniel Park
CTO, Medicore Labs

Subject: Re: Production tail latency surge & fair-share collapse on Medicore VPC

Daniel — thanks for the quick flag. We're on it. Short triage summary and immediate mitigations we will attempt in the next 30 minutes:

1) Immediate: temporarily reduce per-node concurrency and disable large-batch fusion for the affected model to drop tail latency.
2) Mid: perform a rolling restart of the runtime on the hot shard(s) to clear KV cache growth.
3) Fallback: enable model-variant fallback to the quantized variant for high-latency requests and route critical traffic to Redwood-hosted pool if needed.
4) Exec: I will send a brief to Medicore execs and loop in our VP of Customer Success (Laura) for credits/compensatory options.

Marissa and Jonas — can you take point on steps 1–3 and post findings (kernel/alloc logs + autoscaler events) into the JIRA below? We need a pager-friendly root cause in under 2 hours and an action plan for tomorrow (kernel/profile change or rollback).

I'll prepare an executive note for Medicore and include an MA plan link.

Hannah Schmitt
Account Lead — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Quick update from SRE triage — findings and recommended immediate remediation: 

Findings (first-pass):
- The hot shard shows sustained KV-cache growth for a subset of long-context requests. Eviction not keeping up.
- Autoscaler attempted to add two nodes at 13:26 but the fair-share allocator rejected them: quota check flagged (we hit a soft tenant concurrency cap due to policy change last week).
- The runtime build on these nodes had a new kernel selection heuristic deployed in last night's canary (build r2025.9.17-k4) — we see suboptimal attention kernels for sequences >2k causing CPU stalls during decode and therefore request pileup.
- 502s are correlated with request timeouts at the runtime layer, not upstream network.

Immediate remediation (we will execute now):
- Manually increase dedicated node count for Medicore VPC by +3 while we override the fair-share check (temporary emergency bump).
- Roll back runtime kernel to r2025.9.15 on the two hot nodes to remove the heuristic causing stalls.
- Force KV-cache eviction threshold down for 30 minutes to reclaim memory.
- Temporarily disable large-batch fusion for the affected model to reduce per-request latency.

I am attaching the sampled 502 log tails and a small grep of allocator events. If the manual scale and rollback succeed, expect p95 to improve within 10–15 minutes, and p99 to normalize within 30–45 minutes.

Marissa Cole
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachments: medicore-sampled-502-logs-14-20.txt (text), redwood-triage-playbook-MED-001.pdf

Subject: Medicore VPC incident — exec update and immediate plan

Daniel / Medicore execs —

Quick executive summary and our immediate asks / next steps:

What happened: a kernel-selection heuristic introduced in last night's runtime canary caused decode stalls on long-sequence requests; combined with KV-cache growth and a tenant concurrency soft cap, the autoscaler could not add capacity automatically — resulting in latency spike and 5xx amplification.

Actions we have initiated (complete / in-progress):
- Manual emergency scale-up: +3 nodes (in progress).
- Kernel rollback to r2025.9.15 on hot nodes (started).
- KV eviction threshold decreased to force memory reclamation (complete).
- Temporary model-variant fallback to quantized model for latency-sensitive endpoints (complete).
- We have an MA (mutual action) doc open with Medicore operations: MA-Plan link below.

Next 60 minutes: confirm p95/p99 trend and decide on either a permanent rollback or a kernel fix + targeted compile profile. If performance stabilizes, we will schedule a controlled rollout with comprehensive perf regression tests.

Compensation and capacity: Laura (cc'd) is the VP of CS for account compensation discussion; per our SLA we can allocate emergency dedicated capacity and apply a partial credit for the incident window. Laura — please advise on credit and contract-level options so I can communicate to Medicore CTO.

I'll keep this channel updated every ~20 minutes with progress. Thanks for patience — will circle back with a short board-ready timeline once we confirm stabilization.

Hannah Schmitt
Account Lead — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
